title: SKILLLITE: Evidence-Guided Malicious Skill Auditing with Compact LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2609.36879v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: As LLM-based agents perform increasingly complex tasks, Agent Skills have emerged as a flexible mechanism for extending their capabilities. An Agent Skill packages task-specific instructions with executable components and auxiliary resources to provide specialized functionalities. However, the growing adoption of third-party Skills introduces a new supply-chain attack surface. Malicious Skills can embed harmful behaviors that abuse agent privileges and compromise the agent execution environment or accessible resources. Although recent LLM-based malicious Skill auditing approaches have achieved promising performance, they often rely on capable commercial LLMs. How to achieve effective auditing with compact, locally deployable LLMs in security-sensitive and resource-constrained settings remains largely unexplored. translated_title: SKILLLITE：基于证据引导的小型大语言模型恶意技能审计
translated_abstract: 随着基于大语言模型（LLM）的智能体执行越来越复杂的任务，Agent Skills（智能体技能）已成为一种扩展其能力的灵活机制。一个 Agent Skill 将任务特定的指令与可执行组件及辅助资源打包在一起，以提供专门化的功能。然而，第三方 Skills 的日益普及引入了新的供应链攻击面。恶意 Skills 可能嵌入有害行为，滥用智能体权限，从而危害智能体的执行环境或其可访问的资源。尽管近期基于 LLM 的恶意 Skill 审计方法已取得了可喜的性能，但它们通常依赖于能力强大的商业 LLM。如何在安全敏感和资源受限的环境中，使用紧凑的、可本地部署的 LLM 实现有效审计，在很大程度上仍未被探索。我们的研究表明，紧凑型 LLM 难以识别隐藏在复杂 Skill 包中的恶意行为。
tldr: 本文提出SKILLLITE框架，通过证据引导的审计方式，使小型可本地部署的大语言模型也能有效识别Agent Skill中的恶意行为，解决了安全敏感和资源受限场景下第三方技能供应链攻击的检测难题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes SKILLLITE, an evidence-guided auditing framework that enables compact, locally deployable LLMs to effectively detect malicious behaviors hidden in Agent Skills, addressing supply-chain attack risks in security-sensitive and resource-constrained settings.
